name: web-app
title: Web app
summary: For building a web app with AI agents. One agent builds each change, a second checks it against your rules before it reaches main, and only your decisions reach you.

rules.text: Every change ships with a test that fails without it.
rules.why: a test that passes either way proves nothing.

rules.text: Main only moves when the whole test suite passes.
rules.why: two changes can each pass alone and still break each other.

rules.text: Every page works at phone width before it ships.
rules.why: a page that only works on a laptop is a bug nobody reports.

rules.text: Secrets never appear in code, logs or commits.
rules.why: a key pushed once stays public, even after you delete it.

rules.text: A new dependency comes with a one-line reason.
rules.why: every package you add is code you now maintain.

rules.text: An error a person sees says what to do next.
rules.why: "something went wrong" is a support ticket waiting to happen.

rules.text: Tests bind a local port, so a sandboxed agent asks the person instead of rewriting the tests.
rules.why: a test rewritten into a fake passes inside the sandbox and proves nothing about the real server.

choices: It runs on a preview link
questions.default: It runs on a preview link

items.title: Set up the test runner with one passing test
items.criterion: npm test runs the project's test runner and passes, with one real test in test/smoke.test.js that checks the app starts. Before this item npm test has no runner to start, so it fails.
items.brief:
Files:
- package.json (its test script)
- test/smoke.test.js
Test:
- test/smoke.test.js checks the app starts
Use the test runner your framework recommends, and give it a one-line reason (W5).

items.title: The home page works at phone width
items.criterion: The home page shows all of its content at 375 pixels wide without sideways scrolling. test/home-phone-width.test.js checks the page at that width and fails before the change.
items.brief:
Files:
- the home page
- test/home-phone-width.test.js
Test:
- test/home-phone-width.test.js renders the home page 375 pixels wide and fails when anything scrolls sideways

items.title: Every change gets a preview link
items.criterion: Every pull request gets a preview link from the host the deploy question names. test/preview-config.test.js reads the deploy settings, checks that previews are turned on, and fails before the change.
items.brief:
Files:
- the host's deploy settings file
- test/preview-config.test.js
Test:
- test/preview-config.test.js reads the deploy settings and fails when previews are off
